items.title: Incorrect length bound check
items.body: The out-of-bounds check is only done for long-form lengths, and the comparison `length >= limit` is against the whole input rather than the remaining bytes. Short-form lengths are never checked. The subsequent `new byte[length]` in read() can therefore be sized by malformed input, with failure only at EOF. Inside nested decoders, `limit` is the size of the sub-array, which makes the check inconsistent.

items.title: ECDSA tests use one P-256 key and never check JDK verification
items.body: The suite generates a single KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC") key, which is P-256, and uses it for ES256, ES384, and ES512. It only asserts that asn1derToConcatenatedRS and concatenatedRSToASN1DER round-trip through this provider's own decoder. It never calls Signature.verify on the DER produced by concatenatedRSToASN1DER, and ES384/ES512 never see 48-byte or 66-byte R/S values from a matching curve. A DER encoding that Java's strict verifier rejects, or a high-bit padding bug that only shows up at the real ES384/ES512 sizes, still passes.

items.title: Test reuses one EC key for all curves and never verifies
items.body: ECDSAAlgorithmTest generates a single KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC") key (typically P-256) and reuses it for ES256/ES384/ES512, then only asserts round-trip concatenated->DER->concatenated equality. It never verifies the signature with Signature.verify, so wrong signLength padding, truncation, or interop failures against real verifiers are not detected.

items.title: Downsize return value ignored and SVG/vector images corrupted
items.body: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb line 67 calls OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...) in a loop without checking its boolean return. If convert fails the code retries 4 more times then uploads the original oversized file anyway. Worse, the guard uses FileHelper.is_image?(filename) which includes SVG, but OptimizedImage.create_for explicitly skips resizing SVG by just copying it because vector-to-raster convert with -resize/[0] mangles or fails on SVG. Downsizing SVG in place can corrupt it or needlessly rasterize it. Skip SVG and break on false return.

items.title: URL download limit hardcoded to 10MB regardless of upload type or settings
items.body:
API URL uploads are now capped at a fixed 10MB instead of following site settings. Two effects:
- Admins who raised `max_image_size_kb` or `max_attachment_size_kb` above 10MB can no longer upload such files by URL.
- Attachments up to 10MB are downloaded even when the configured attachment limit is far smaller, wasting bandwidth before the inevitable rejection.

items.title: Unsubscribe does not mute watched or tracked topics
items.body: When the user is watching or tracking this topic, this branch changes the level to `regular`, not `muted`. Regular topics can still generate direct reply and mention notifications, so the email link's promise to stop notifications is not met for these users. Set the level to muted for this unsubscribe action.

items.title: A GET unsubscribe link toggles state on every visit
items.body: This action is exposed only as GET, but it mutates the user's notification setting, and the operation toggles between muted and regular. Reopening or refreshing the email link can therefore undo the unsubscribe and resume notifications. Make the operation idempotently set muted, and avoid changing notification state on a GET request.

items.title: Early interpolation defeats $__range no-split guard
items.body: runSplitQuery() now calls datasource.applyTemplateVariables() before querySupportsSplitting(). querySupportsSplitting() excludes queries where isQueryWithRangeVariable(query.expr) is true because $__range must be interpolated per split chunk on the backend. After up-front interpolation the expr no longer contains $__range, so the check never fires, the query is time-split, and every chunk keeps the full-range value baked in at line 296-300. The result is wrong $__range_s/$__range_ms values in split sub-queries.

items.title: Empty-expr filter now runs before interpolation
items.body: Previously `interpolateVariablesInQueries` ran first and the `query.expr` filter ran on the interpolated result. Now the filter runs on the raw expr and interpolation happens afterwards. A query whose expr is just a variable that resolves to an empty string is no longer dropped and gets sent for execution and sharding. The same ordering applies in `runSplitQuery`. Filter on the interpolated expr instead.

items.title: Non-boolean flag exported
items.body: `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is a `string | undefined` (the secret itself) rather than a boolean. It is easy to misuse or leak, so wrap it in `!!(...)`.

items.title: createErrorResponse() calls setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError() unconditionally, hiding the username field even for first-time (non re-authentication) logins after a passkey error
items.body: WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse() now calls AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError(context) on every passkey error. That utility (AuthenticatorUtils.java lines 125-133) sets LoginFormsProvider.USERNAME_HIDDEN=true and REGISTRATION_DISABLED=true only when the auth note USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH is 'true'. The note is set in UsernamePasswordForm.authenticate() only when context.getUser() != null (line 102). However, this authenticator is also used from UsernameForm flows and potentially other flows where the note may be stale: the note is removed in UsernamePasswordForm.authenticate() only in the `else` branch (line 104), but if a previous authentication attempt in the same authentication session set the note (e.g. user was identified, then the flow restarted or a different authenticator ran), the note can persist and cause the username field to be hidden on a subsequent error page even though the current challenge is for a fresh login where the user must type their username. More concretely: in the UsernameForm flow (PasskeysUsernameFormTest), after the user submits a username, the PasswordForm runs; if a passkey error occurs there, createErrorResponse() is invoked and — because the note was never set in that flow (UsernameForm does not set USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH) — the utility correctly does nothing. But in the UsernamePasswordForm flow, if the user first fails a password (note set, username hidden), then the passkey conditional UI errors, the error page keeps the username hidden — which is intended. The risk is that the note is session-scoped and not cleared when the authentication session restarts the flow (e.g. after a 'try again' or restart), so a stale 'true' note can hide the username on a fresh login form. The utility should be defensive, but more importantly the note lifecycle is not reset when the user is cleared (context.clearUser() in AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.badPasswordHandler clears the user but not the note), so a user who fails password (note set), then somehow gets the user cleared and re-enters a username, would see a hidden username field with no way to correct it. This is a real UX/data-integrity edge case introduced by relying on a note that is not cleared in lockstep with the user.

items.title: create ignores alias_level sent by the form
items.body: The new form shows the alias level combo-box when creating a group, and `asJSON` sends `alias_level`, but `create` only sets `name` and `visible`. Any alias level chosen at creation is silently discarded until the group is saved again.

cal.com__11059.text: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

discourse-graphite__1.text: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.

Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).

Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.

discourse-graphite__2.text: logic: Potential nil pointer exception - if no TopicUser record exists, tu will be nil and calling methods on it will crash
Typo in property name: 'stopNotificiationsText' should be 'stopNotificationsText' (missing 'n' in 'Notifications')

discourse-graphite__8.text: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.

In the next action, capping the next offset at user_count can produce an empty page (e.g., total equal to limit results in offset == total, showing 2/2 with no members). This can cause confusing UX on the last page.
The remove_member test uses xhr :put to call the remove_member action, but the route defines delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member' requiring DELETE method.

The `totalPages` calculation using `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` produces an extra page when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`, leading to incorrect pagination. For example, with 100 users and a limit of 50, it reports 3 pages instead of 2, allowing navigation to an empty page.
Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined

The route provides the group's ID in params[:id], but the code attempts to read it from params[:group_id], causing the action to fail. This results in a broken feature when trying to access group memberships.

grafana__107534.text: The applyTemplateVariables method is called with request.filters as the third parameter, but this parameter is not used in the corresponding test setup.

keycloak-greptile__1.text: In UsernameForm.authenticate(), isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() is called without passing the required UserModel parameter.

With isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) requiring user != null, authenticate(...) will not call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) on the initial login page where context.getUser() is still null, so conditional passkey UI will not be set up for first-time passkey login. Consider whether this should also be enabled when no user has been selected yet so ID-less passkey authentication on the initial login form continues to work.

keycloak__33832.text: Returns wrong provider (default keystore instead of BouncyCastle)

Dead code exists where ASN1Encoder instances are created and written to, but their results are immediately discarded. The actual encoding is performed by new ASN1Encoder instances created in the subsequent return statement, rendering the earlier operations useless.
When length starts at -1 from indefinite-length encoding, the arithmetic 'length = length - bytes.length' will behave unexpectedly, potentially leading to incorrect processing of encoded data.
Abstract order() method on CryptoProvider may break backward compatibility with existing implementations
